results.title: Virtual Museums as Meaning-Modeling Systems in Digital ...
results.content: # Virtual Museums as Meaning-Modeling Systems in Digital Heritage This article frames the virtual museum as a meaning-modeling system within digital heritage and proposes an operational semiotic method for analysis. digital heritage; virtual museum; modeling systems theory; semiotics; subject–object relation; quantitative content analysis; non-identity Specifically, the study draws on Thomas Sebeok’s Modeling Systems Theory (MST) [28] and Theodor Adorno’s dialectical philosophy [29] to explore the theoretical underpinnings of virtual museums. MST elucidates how human cognition and social activity are mediated through forms of meaning [28], a principle directly aligned with the objectives of this research, to determine how the virtual museum system functions as a human representation. With this clarified understanding, we move on to articulate the theoretical framework and methodology by which we analyze how virtual museums model meaning and how non-identity manifests in digital cultural spaces. We use virtual museum experience as an umbrella term for curated digital experiences with museological intent, including web interactives, 360 tours, VR/AR applications, and 3D simulations.

results.content: **ENGL 1105 -** **FWS: Writing and Sexual Politics** **(3 Credits)** **ENGL 1111 -** **FWS: Writing Across Cultures** **(3 Credits)** **ENGL 1120 -** **FWS: Writing and Community Engagement** **(3 Credits)** This course enables students to read, write, and design forms of communication that engage with the environment, in order to inform, advocate, and to connect with our world. **ENGL 1131 -** **FWS: Mastering College Reading and Writing** **(3 Credits)** In each section of this course, students receive extensive guidance from their instructors in the discovery and practice of helpful methods for fully exploring and appreciating what they read as well as guidance in planning, drafting, and writing essays about what is read and discussed in class. **ENGL 1167 -** **FWS: Reading Now** **(3 Credits)** In this class, we will engage with widely varied cultural forms-including, perhaps, experimental poetry, medieval manuscripts, graphic novels, memoirs, plays, films, podcasts, and more-to develop multiple media literacies as we sharpen our own writing about culture, literature, and art.
